title.narrative: Lifesaving Protection, WASH, NFIs, Health and Nutrition Assistance to Displacement and Famine in Tawila, North Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtNorth Darfur State currently hosts 14% of the IDP caseload in Sudan (IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix, update Aug 2024). The influx of displaced people in North Darfur is straining food security and nutrition, especially for vulnerable groups, such as children. Food is available but not affordable for the majority of IDP and host community households and they face barriers to accessing healthcare, protection, shelter and other basic services due to the disruption of supplies, infrastructure damages, displacements, and imposed restrictions.ltbrgtSave the Children (SC), in consortium with PLAN International and Saeker Voluntary Organization, aim to support the most vulnerable children and families to meet basic needs and reduce high morbidity, acute malnutrition, disease outbreaks and exposure to protection risks by increasing access to integrated, disability-inclusive and gender-sensitive health, nutrition, Shelter/NFI, and protection services in Tawila Locality. To achieve this, under the leadership of Save the Children (SC), the Consortium will contribute to improving equitable and inclusive access to quality life-saving curative and preventative healthcare services through three health facilities in Tawila, covering prioritized locations with the most vulnerable populations.nbspTo fill identified health and nutrition gaps including medical supplies, incentives, minor rehabilitation and referrals and increase the coverage, the project will target women of reproductive age, with a focus on pregnant and lactating women, and children under 5 years of age, while providing gender-sensitive and disability-inclusive lifesaving healthcare for communicable and non-communicable diseases among children over 5, adults and the elderly. The proposed health interventions will provide essential maternal and child health services, essential medication, and supplies (PPE, diagnostics, case management), establish referral pathways and strengthen the immunization services.ltbrgtSC will also provide emergency lifesaving nutrition services directly targeting 6,776 of beneficiariesnbsp(2,245 girls,2156 boys, 2,235 women,139 men)nbspwith an emphasis on increasing access for conflict-affected people in Tawila, including community management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) and preventive nutrition services. The project will be securing nutrition supplies, contributing to facilities running cost, and establishing linkages between stabilization centers, OTP and TSFP sites. Emphasis will also be given to preventive nutrition services of IYCF community-based support of IYCF through mother support groups, andnbsp (IYCF-E) with focus on one-to-one IYCF counseling and support for mothers, promotion of breastfeeding and hygiene.ltbrgtUnder the Shelter/NFI component, Plan International will provide NFI and shelter to support essential daily activities and offer adaptable shelter solutions to 11,301 people. This will include life-saving in-kind non-food items to the most vulnerable IDPs and host communities, distribute cash for shelter/NFIs to assist affected households to establish or rehabilitate shelters, supply and construct emergency shelter with high-standards and provide materials for the construction of emergency shelter. ltbrgtLastly, under the leadership of Saeker Voluntary Organization, the Consortium will provide an integrated GBV, CP and GP response to conflict-affected communities in Tawila locality, including children, women and people with disabilities. The project will conduct regular protection monitoring. CBPNs members and active community members will be trained and actively engaged in the protection monitoring. Saeker Voluntary Organization will provide mental health and psycho-social support services including provision of psychological first aid, social and life skills interventions and recreational for GBV Survivors, elderly, female head household, elderly. The project will also train service providers on, in particular, legal, health and social care providers on PSEA.ltbrgtlt/pgt
